title: Multiplexer
body:
A **multiplexer** (MUX) is a [[Combinational Logic|combinational]] selector: $2^n$ data
inputs, $n$ select lines, one output. The select lines are read as a binary number and the
input with that index is passed through. It is a hardware `switch` statement, or an array
index.

A 4-to-1 MUX with selects $S_1 S_0$:

| $S_1$ | $S_0$ | Output |
|:-:|:-:|---|
| 0 | 0 | $I_0$ |
| 0 | 1 | $I_1$ |
| 1 | 0 | $I_2$ |
| 1 | 1 | $I_3$ |

$$Y = \bar{S_1}\bar{S_0}I_0 + \bar{S_1}S_0I_1 + S_1\bar{S_0}I_2 + S_1S_0I_3$$

Run it backwards (one input, $n$ selects, $2^n$ outputs) and you have a
**demultiplexer**, which is a [[Decoder]] with an enable input.

Multiplexers are everywhere inside a [[CPU]]: choosing which register feeds the
[[ALU]], choosing between an immediate value and a register operand, choosing the next
program counter. They are also how many devices share one [[System Bus]].
